newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker rates static after lacklustre week.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker rates static after lacklustre week.

text.p: World crude tanker rates finished barely changed on Friday as the absence of U.S. players took its toll on an already lacklustre market.
Brokers in London said their phones stayed quiet all day, as offices in the United States remained closed for the Independence Day holiday.
But if volume was hit hard, most rates held up, ending broadly in line with last week.
Brokers said the Mediterranean sector was the most active of the last few days, with aframax rates holding firm around W120.
Million-barrel vessels cross-Med fared less well, with last week's spot low becoming this week's norm, and most suezmax fixtures settled at or below W80.
The number of overall VLCC fixtures slipped below average this week, putting pressure on owners of older ships looking for July fixings. Brokers said confidence had also ebbed among suezmax owners.
Brokers said availability of ULCC tankers was "building up ominously" after an extremely quiet week.
Middle East business was plagued by falling freight levels and a number of cancellations due to bad weather in the East.
Nevertheless, rates held up, with Mideast/West VLCC fixtures seen at W52.5 and voyages to Singapore at W54.
"Enquiry improved this week, but freight levels continued to fall because of the build up of available tonnage," said a broker.
Brokers noted a widening gap between older and more modern vessels, with the fixing of the 265,000 tonne Ellen Maersk to Tokyo at W70 demonstrating the strong market for modern tankers.
Similarly, Mideast rates to South Korea were assessed between W57 and W67 depending on the ship's age.
In the western hemisphere, West Africa saw a busier week. Charterers maintained West Africa/U.S. Gulf rates around W82-87 for suezmaxes, depending on the age of vessels, and at W65 for VLCCs.
Carib rates for aframaxes looked healthier than in other regions, but were still flagging below W155 compared with last week's W170 level.
"Tonnage trading in the Caribbean did suffer expected losses," said a broker at Galbraith's in London, noting that he had seen rates for 70,000 tonnes as low as W145.
In the North Sea, suezmax rates firmed slightly to W102 while aframax rates slipped to W117.5.
Slight gains were made on UK continent charters to the United States, with aframax fixtures up slightly at W125.
